# App frame and page layout

From [the component index](../components.md). A prop with `?` is optional, and `= x` is its default. An indented line is the shape of a value the prop takes. In the examples, `children`, `transactions`, the icons and the handlers stand for the screen's own content, data and state.

## TabView, TabViewBrand

```tsx
import { TabView } from "@tuja/ui/components/tab-view";
import { TabViewBrand } from "@tuja/ui/components/tab-view-brand";
```

The frame of an app with top-level destinations: a rail or sidebar from `md`, a tab bar below it. Wrap every screen in one.

Give `header` a `TabViewBrand`, also exported from `tab-view`: the app's mark, name and detail line, of which the icon rail shows only the mark. `TabViewLabelsOnly` from `tab-view` shows any other children only in the labelled sidebar.

### TabView

Props (also `css`):

- `children: ReactNode` — The screen of the current destination.
- `label: string` — Accessible name for the `<nav>` landmark of the rail and of the tab bar, already localised.
- `linkComponent?: ComponentType<TabViewLinkProps> = <a>` — Renders each destination, in the rail and in the tab bar.
- `rail?: "icons" | "labels" | "auto" = "auto"` — How the rail shows the destinations at `md` and wider.
- `header?: ReactNode` — The top of the rail, such as the app's mark.
- `footer?: ReactNode` — The bottom of the rail, such as the signed-in member.
- `secondary?: ReactNode` — A second list under the destinations, such as the reports of this month.
- `effect?: "liquid" | "none" = "liquid"` — An effect the effect layer draws on the indicator of the current destination.
- `as?: "main" | "div" = "main"` — Landmark element for the content.
- `items: readonly TabViewItem[] | readonly PlainTabViewItem[]` — The destinations, in order, each with the `href`, `label`, `icon` and `skeleton` of its screen.
  - `TabViewItem { skeleton: ReactElement; href: string; label: ReactNode; icon: Icon; current?: boolean; badge?: ReactNode; count?: number; status?: ReactNode }`
  - `PlainTabViewItem { skeleton?: undefined; href: string; label: ReactNode; icon: Icon; current?: boolean; badge?: ReactNode; count?: number; status?: ReactNode }`
- `linkStatus?: ComponentType<TabLinkStatusProps> | null = null` — A component that the view renders inside each destination link, so that a router hook can read whether the navigation to it is pending.
- `fallbackSkeleton?: ReactElement` — What shows on a page outside every destination.

### TabViewBrand

Props (also `css`):

- `name: string` — The app's name, beside the mark in the labelled sidebar.
- `detail?: ReactNode` — A muted line under the name, such as the household or the account the app shows.
- `mark?: ReactNode` — The app's mark. Defaults to a square solid `Avatar` of `name`; pass `initials` to choose its letters, or a node of your own, such as a logo.
- `initials?: string` — The letters of the default mark, such as `"Qi"`.

Example:

```tsx
function TabViewExample() {
  return (
    <TabView
      label="Assistant"
      items={[
        { href: "/today", label: "Today", icon: SunIcon, current: true },
        { href: "/todos", label: "To-dos", icon: CheckSquareIcon, count: 17 },
        { href: "/settings", label: "Settings", icon: GearSixIcon },
      ]}
      header={
        <TabViewBrand name="Assistant" initials="Qi" detail="2 mailboxes" />
      }
      css={pageColumn.list}
    >
      {children}
    </TabView>
  );
}
```

## NavigationSplitView

```tsx
import { NavigationSplitView } from "@tuja/ui/components/navigation-split-view";
```

The columns of one screen inside a `TabView`: an optional sidebar (a list of accounts, settings sections), the content, and an optional detail. Use it with `content` alone for a one-pane screen.

A `"page"` sidebar or a `skeleton` needs a router: pass `linkStatus` and `skeleton`. With `linkStatus={null}`, use a `"hidden"` or `"drawer"` sidebar or a `detail`.

Props (also `css`):

- `content: NavigationSplitViewColumn` — The middle column, such as one account and its ledger.
  - `NavigationSplitViewColumn { node: ReactNode; label: string; key?: string | null; back?: SplitViewBackLink | null; accessory?: ReactNode }`
- `linkComponent?: ComponentType<SplitViewLinkProps> = <a>` — Renders each back link and each `SplitViewLink`.
- `replace?: (href: string) => void = location.replace` — Replaces the current history entry with `href`, as a router's `replace` does.
- `sidebar?: NavigationSplitViewSidebar | NavigationSplitViewSidebarWithoutPage | null` — The first column, such as a list of accounts.
- `detail?: NavigationSplitViewDetail | null` — The last column, such as the editor of a picked transaction.
  - `NavigationSplitViewDetail { back: SplitViewBackLink; closeLabel: string; node: ReactNode; label: string; key?: string | null }`
- `linkStatus?: ComponentType<TabLinkStatusProps> | null = null` — A component that the view renders inside each `SplitViewLink`, so that a router hook can read whether the navigation to it is pending.
- `skeleton?: ReactElement` — What the content column shows after a moment of waiting, in the shape of the content.

Example:

```tsx
function NavigationSplitViewExample() {
  return (
    <NavigationSplitView
      css={pageColumn.settings}
      linkComponent={Link}
      linkStatus={LinkStatus}
      skeleton={sectionSkeleton}
      sidebar={{
        stacked: "page",
        href: "/settings",
        label: "Settings",
        node: <nav aria-label="Settings">{children}</nav>,
      }}
      content={{
        label: "Household",
        back: { href: "/settings", label: "Settings" },
        node: children,
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

## HeaderFooterLayout

```tsx
import { HeaderFooterLayout } from "@tuja/ui/components/header-footer-layout";
```

The shell of a reading page with no app frame: floating header controls at the top, the content, a footer.

Props (also `css`):

- `children: ReactNode` — Page content. Flows up past the header controls by default, so a hero or backdrop bleeds to the top edge; a text-first page adds its own clearance.
- `headerStart?: ReactNode` — Start (leading) floating group at the top of the page, typically a back or home link.
- `headerEnd?: ReactNode` — End (trailing) floating group at the top of the page, typically utility controls such as a theme toggle or language picker.
- `background?: ReactNode` — Full-bleed decoration behind the content and beneath the header controls, such as gradients, glows or texture.
- `footer?: ReactNode` — Footer element, rendered at the bottom of the page in the page column.
- `pageColumn?: boolean` — Sets the content in the page column, on the same edges as the header controls and the footer.
- `contentMaxInlineSize?: string` — Narrows the page column below the site default (prose-heavy pages).
- `wideHeader?: boolean` — Sets the header controls on the wide page column, one page gutter from the screen edges, so they line up with a gallery that runs wide (`pageColumn.wide`).
- `as?: "main" | "div" = "main"` — Landmark element for the content region.

Example:

```tsx
function HeaderFooterLayoutExample() {
  return (
    <HeaderFooterLayout
      pageColumn
      headerStart={
        <Button href="/" look="ghost" size="sm">
          Home
        </Button>
      }
      footer={
        <Text look="caption" tone="muted">
          © 2026
        </Text>
      }
    >
      {children}
    </HeaderFooterLayout>
  );
}
```

## StickyControls, StickyControlGroup

```tsx
import { StickyControls } from "@tuja/ui/components/sticky-controls";
import { StickyControlGroup } from "@tuja/ui/components/sticky-control-group";
```

A filter bar that sticks under the header while the page scrolls; one group per cluster of controls.

### StickyControls

Props (also `css`):

- `children: ReactNode` — The row's groups — a `StickyControlGroup` per cluster of controls.

### StickyControlGroup

Props (also `css`):

- `children: ReactNode` — The controls in the group — a media type toggle, a sort picker, a reset.

## Layout primitives

StyleX style objects for the space between components. Compose them in `css`: `<div css={stack.group}>`, `<div css={[row.inline, styles.mine]}>`.

```tsx
import { pageColumn } from "@tuja/ui/primitives/page-column.stylex";
import { show } from "@tuja/ui/primitives/show.stylex";
import { stack, cluster, row } from "@tuja/ui/primitives/stack.stylex";
import { flex } from "@tuja/ui/primitives/flex.stylex";
```

- `pageColumn.{base,scroller,wide,regular,list,settings,report}` from `@tuja/ui/primitives/page-column.stylex`: The page column's width. Give `pageColumn.list`, `settings` or `report` to the `css` of a `TabView` or `NavigationSplitView`; compose `base` on a box of your own.
- `show.{fromMd,belowMd}` from `@tuja/ui/primitives/show.stylex`: Show a box only on a wide `TabView` (`show.fromMd`) or only on a phone (`show.belowMd`), such as a `Table` that is a `List` on a phone. Put it on a wrapper.
- `stack.{text,rows,tight,item,group,section}` from `@tuja/ui/primitives/stack.stylex`: A column that owns the gap between its children: `section` between page blocks, `group` between cards, `item` inside a card, `tight` for a heading over its text.
- `cluster.{inline,tight,item}` from `@tuja/ui/primitives/stack.stylex`: A row that wraps, such as a line of badges or buttons.
- `row.{inline,tight,item}` from `@tuja/ui/primitives/stack.stylex`: A row that does not wrap, such as an icon beside its label or the buttons of a header.
- `flex.{row,col,center,between,wrap,inlineCenter}` from `@tuja/ui/primitives/flex.stylex`: A bare flex box with no gap; change one property after it with `align`, `justify`, `grow` or `shrink` from the same file.
